title: GCP Cloud Run Cold Start Rate

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.3.24 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.3.24 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:monitoring` collected via Custom (GCP Monitoring API); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: Serverless cold start impact on request latency. High cold start rates cause P99 latency spikes and timeouts for scale-to-zero services.
value: Detecting gcp cloud run cold start rate early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Use GCP Monitoring API (or Cloud Monitoring export) to ingest Cloud Run metrics. Request count and instance count indicate scale-to-zero; zero instances with requests implies cold starts. For detailed latency, ingest `run.googleapis.com/request_latencies` and `run.googleapis.com/container/startup_latencies`. Alert when cold start rate exceeds 5% or startup latency > 3s. Consider min instances for latency-critical services.
visualization: Line chart (cold start % and startup latency by service over time), Table (service, cold starts, %), Single value (cold start rate).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU

dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure Custom (GCP Monitoring API) with the modular input for `google:gcp:monitoring`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `resource.type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use GCP Monitoring API (or Cloud Monitoring export) to ingest Cloud Run metrics. Request count and instance count indicate scale-to-zero; zero instances with requests implies cold starts. For detailed latency, ingest `run.googleapis.com/request_latencies` and `run.googleapis.com/container/startup_latencies`. Alert when cold start rate exceeds 5% or startup latency > 3s. Consider min instances for latency-critical services.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="run.googleapis.com/request_count" OR metric.type="run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.24_gcp_cloud_run_cold_start_24"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:monitoring` in `index=gcp` to detect gcp cloud run cold start rate. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `resource.type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_24_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (cold start % and startup latency by service over time), Table (service, cold starts, %), Single value (cold start rate)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom (GCP Monitoring API) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
